land.text: Sumer: Utu-hengal's kingdom, taken by his 'governor of Ur, Ur-Nammu'
Lagash: 'He slew Nam-ha-ni the ensi of Lagash' (Code of Ur-Nammu)
Akkad, Eshnunna and Akshak, which Kutik-Inshushinak had taken, 'reconquered' by Ur-Nammu, then Susa, 'overrun by the Third dynasty of Ur under Ur-Nammu and his son Shulgi'
Isin and Nippur under Ishbi-Erra, who 'formed an independent kingdom' c. 2018, and the rest of Sumer that 'fell away' before 2004
Ur, sacked and held 'through military occupation for the next 21 years', and Susa
Larsa under Naplanum (r. c. 2025–2005), a vassal dynasty inside the realm

capitals.name: Ur (Tell el-Muqayyar)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Historic seat: Ur'; the text says the kings had no capital 'as such'.

rulers.name: Shulgi
rulers.note: 'He reigned for 48 years, from c. 2094 – c. 2046 BC' (Shulgi page).

rulers.name: Ibbi-Sin
rulers.note: Taken captive to Elam at the fall of Ur.

correction.text: Sumer, 'the heart of the empire, the country (kalam)' divided into about twenty provinces; Lagash added when 'He slew Nam-ha-ni the ensi of Lagash' (c. 2110); Akkad, Eshnunna and Susa followed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for Ur-Nammu's first years, before the title 'King of Sumer and Akkad'. Cliopatria has no Ur III polity.

correction.text: the Ur III realm: the twenty provinces of Sumer and Akkad with the periphery 'from Urbilum to Pashime and Susa', the Diyala valley 'where garrisons were established' and 'the foothills of the Zagros'; Cliopatria labels it Gutian; its years are -2100..-2004, and the ledger's losses shrink it from 2024

keyframe_review.note: 131,488 km2 over Sumer, Akkad and Susiana (bbox 44.2–51.1 E, 30.2–33.4 N), dated -2100..-2001 and mislabelled 'Gutian Dynasty' by Cliopatria: the Gutians ended c. 2119. Used here unchanged with corrected years; the north (Urbilum, Assur, 'possibly Nineveh') is not in the shape and is left as vassal tint (ledger -2049). No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: the Third Dynasty of Ur's realm; Cliopatria's 12,568 km2 'Sumerian City-States' fragment at Ur and Eridu for -2100..-2001 is the heartland of the same state and is superseded by the larger outline

keyframe_review.note: Also reviewed as wrong in sumerian-city-states.

ledger.note: 2112 BCE: Ur-Nammu founds the Third Dynasty of Ur. 'Founded: c. 2112 BC'; Utu-hegal was dethroned by court notables 'headed by Ur-Namma', probably his brother, after about eight years; the History of Sumer page: 'Ur-Nammu of Ur defeated Utu-hegal of Uruk and founded the Third Dynasty of Ur'; the Sumer page: 'in 2112 BC'.

2110 BCE: Ur-Nammu takes Lagash. The Code of Ur-Nammu's prologue: 'He slew Nam-ha-ni the ensi of Lagash'; Nam-mahani 'r. c. 2113 – c. 2110 BC (MC)'. Lagash became 'the largest and most prosperous province of the empire'.

region.text: Akkad, Eshnunna and Akshak, which Kutik-Inshushinak had 'conquered early in Ur-Nammu's reign'

ledger.note: 2100 BCE: Ur-Nammu 'reconquered the northern territories'. He took the title 'King of Sumer and Akkad' 'after extending his domination over Lower Mesopotamia' (Ur III page); no page dates the reconquest within his reign (2112–2094).

2094 BCE: Ur takes Susa. 'Susa was overrun by the Third dynasty of Ur under Ur-Nammu and his son Shulgi'; 'The Ur III dynasty had held control over Susa since the demise of Puzur-Inshushinak' (Shulgi page). Dated to Ur-Nammu's last year; Anshan stayed Elamite.

region.text: the periphery 'from Urbilum to Pashime and Susa', 'the foothills of the Zagros', the Diyala valley 'where garrisons were established'

ledger.counterpart: Zagros highland polities (Simurrum, Lullubum, Urbilum, Karhar)
ledger.note: 2049 BCE: Shulgi's year 45: he 'smashed the heads of Urbilum, Simurrum, Lullubum and Karhar in a single campaign'; Simurrum and Lullubum were destroyed nine times 'between the 26th and 45th years of his reign', Der in year 21, Karhar in 24 and 31, Harshi in 27, Kimash and Hurti in 45–46. A tribute belt under garrisons, drawn as the lighter tint (rule 4).

2025 BCE: Naplanum rules Larsa inside the realm. 'Naplanum: r. c. 2025 – c. 2005 BC (MC)' heads the Larsa king list while Ur still ruled Sumer; drawn as Ur's vassal until the fall of Ur. The page does not call him a vassal; bridged.

2024 BCE: Lagash stops dating by Ur. 'After the fifth year of the last Ur III ruler, Ibbi-Sin, his year name was no longer used at Lagash', which 'indicates Ur had lost control'. Who held it is not on the page.

ledger.counterpart: Zagros highland polities (Simurrum, Lullubum, Urbilum, Karhar)
ledger.note: 2020 BCE: the tribute belt lapses. Under Ibbi-Sin 'The incursions of the Amorite tribes are increasingly violent', the archives 'dried up from the beginning of his reign (after the third year)' and 'Eshnunna and especially Isin became independent'. Year bridged.
2020 BCE: Eshnunna is independent. 'Eshnunna and especially Isin became independent' under Ibbi-Sin; no year on the page. Eshnunna needs a dossier.

region.text: 'The province of Isin broke out and formed an independent kingdom under Ishbi-Erra'

ledger.note: 2018 BCE: Ishbi-Erra makes Isin independent. 'The First Dynasty of Isin was founded by Ishbi-Erra (r. 2018-1985 BCE)'; his own page: he was assigning 'his own regnal year-names' 'by Ibbi-Sin's 8th year' (c. 2021 by Ibbi-Sin's dates). Ishbi-Erra 'was described as a man of Mari', an official of Ibbi-Sin.

2015 BCE: Susa slips from Ur. Ibbi-Sin's campaigns 'against Anshan, Huhnur, and Susa ceased after his fourteenth year of reign' (2028 − 14); 'A new political power, the Shimashki dynasty, took power in Anshan and Elam'.

region.text: the Sumerian provinces outside Ur: Uruk, Umma, Eridu

ledger.note: 2008 BCE: the provinces fall away. Cities 'fell away', 'notably Isin under the Amorite ruler Ishbi-Erra', and Ibbi-Sin was left 'with only the city of Ur' by the end of his reign. Year and counterpart bridged; the Isin page says the Elamites 'attacked Isin and Ur'.
2004 BCE: Larsa's dynasty outlives its suzerain. 'After the Third Dynasty of Ur collapsed c. 2004 BC', Larsa's kings continue (Naplanum to 2005, then his successors).

region.text: Ur, the capital and its district, 'with only the city of Ur' (Ibbi-Sin page)

ledger.note: 2004 BCE: Ur falls to the Elamites and Shimashki. 'The kingdom of Ur was destroyed around 2004 BC by an Elamite army', 'a coalition of Elamite troops, including people from Anshan and Shimashki'; 'Elam, along with tribesmen from the region of Shimashki in the Zagros Mountains sacked Ur and took Ibbi-Sin captive' under Kindattu, 'taken to the land Elam in fetters' (Ibbi-Sin page, which also offers 1940 BC short chronology). Ur was 'ruled through military occupation for the next 21 years' (Shimashki page).

wars.name: Shulgi's Zagros and Elamite campaigns

zones.text: the Zagros foothills from Der to Urbilum

wars.outcome: Year names: Der destroyed (21), Karhar (24, 31), Simurrum (25, 27, 32, nine times to 44), Harshi (27), Anshan (34, after the governor of Anshan married the king's daughter in 30), the wall of the land built (37) against 'the Tidnumite nomads', Shashrum (42), Urbilum, Simurrum, Lullubum and Karhar 'in a single campaign' (45), Kimash and Hurti (45–46). A tribute periphery, not annexation.

wars.name: Shu-Sin's campaign against Zabshali and Shimashki
wars.outcome: 'Year Shu-Sin, the king of Ur, king of the four quarters, destroyed the land of Zabshali' (his sixth year); authority asserted in Shimanum, Zabshali and Shimashki; 'a new wall' built against the Amorites. No border moved.

wars.name: Fall of Ur
wars.outcome: The provinces fell away to Isin and the Amorites; the Elamite and Shimashki army under Kindattu sacked Ur c. 2004, took Ibbi-Sin captive and garrisoned the city for about twenty years.
wars.note: Ibbi-Sin's year 17 is named for the Amorites' submission; the Elamite blow came after.

certainty.note: The core is a dated administrative record ('about twenty provinces', year names, the bala) but no boundary survey; the periphery 'from Urbilum to Pashime and Susa' is a tribute belt with garrisons and is drawn soft; 'the wall of the land' (Shulgi 37) and Shu-Sin's 'new wall' are the one built line, against the Amorites north of Akkad.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks as its own entry, although it draws it: the 131,488 km2 shape labelled 'Gutian Dynasty' for -2100..-2001 is Ur III's realm (Sumer, Akkad, Susiana) and is used here with the years -2100..-2004; a new keyframe covers 2112–2101 on Sumer. The 'Sumerian City-States' fragment of the same years is marked wrong. Both Cliopatria Names are listed in cliopatria_names so the validator accepts the shape ids; the other shapes of those Names belong to other dossiers and the warnings are expected.

Chronology: middle chronology throughout (Ur-Nammu 2112–2094, Ibbi-Sin 2028–2004); the pages also give short-chronology figures (Ur III c. 2047–1940, Tirigan c. 2055). Shulgi's year n is 2094 − n + 1. The Isin page's 2018 for Ishbi-Erra is used for the split; his own page's 'Ibbi-Sin's 8th year' would be c. 2021.

Bridged (confidence 1): Ur-Nammu's reconquest of Akkad and Eshnunna (-2100) and of Susa (-2094), Larsa as a vassal dynasty (-2025..-2004), the lapse of the Zagros tribute belt (-2020), Eshnunna's independence (-2020), the provinces falling away (-2008). Eshnunna, Der, Simurrum, Lullubum, Urbilum and Karhar have no dossiers; Assur and 'possibly Nineveh' were dominated 'for a time' (undated; left to me-02's assyria). The Elamite occupation of Ur after 2004 is in the elam dossier (-2004..-1983). Isin, Larsa, Der, Eshnunna are not in the gazetteer; Nippur, Ur, Lagash are.
